title: 10X Genomics Single-Nucleus RNA-Sequencing for Transcriptomic Profiling of Adult Human Tissues
author: Sarah Urata
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.86khzcw
materials: Count nuclei (e.g. BioRad T20 Cell Counter)

Prepare Reagents for use Equilibrate gel beads to room temperature for 00:30:00 . Thaw, vortex, and centrifuge RT Reagent, Template Switch Oligo, and Reducing Agent B. Verify no precipitate in Reducing Agent B. Centrifuge RT Enzyme C before adding to Master Mix.
GEM-RT Incubation Incubate in a thermocycler to complete reverse transcription. Store at 4 °C for up to 72:00:00 or at -20 °C for up to a week. Or proceed to the next step.

Post GEM-RT Cleanup & cDNA Amplification - Prepare Reagents for use Thaw, vortex, and centrifuge a tube of Reducing Agent B and cDNA primers. Maintain Amp Mix on ice after vortex and centrifuge Thaw Cleanup Buffer at 65 °C for 00:10:00 with shaking at max rpm then cool to room temperature.

cDNA Amplification Prepare cDNA Amplification Mix on ice. Vortex and centrifuge briefly. Add 65 µL cDNA Amplification Reaction Mix to 35 µL sample. Pipette mix 15x to mix and centrifuge briefly. Incubate in a thermocycler to amplify cDNA. Use cycle number optimization table for total number of cycles When using nuclei, increase the optimized number of cycles by one cycle Maximum: load 1600 nuclei - perform 12 cycles

cDNA Cleanup --SPRIselect Perform a 0.6X beads purification with SPRIselect reagent Wash twice with freshly prepared 80% ethanol Elute with 40.5 µL Qiagen Buffer EB. Transfer 40 µL to a new strip tube. Store at 4 °C for up to 72:00:00 or at -20 °C for up to 4 weeks. Or proceed to the next step.
Prepare Reagents for use Thaw, vortex, and centrifuge Fragmentation Buffer, Adaptor Oligos, Ligation Buffer, SI Primer. Maintain on ice Fragmentation Enzyme, DNA Ligase, and Amp Mix.

Post Fragmentation, End Repair & A-tailing Double Sided Size Selection --SPRIselect Vortex to resuspend the SPRIselect reagent. Add 30 µL SPRIselect reagent (0.6X) to each sample and pipette mix 15x. Incubate 00:05:00 at room temperature. Centrifuge briefly Place sample on magnetic separator. DO NOT discard supernatant. Transfer 75 µL supernatant to a new tube strip tube. Vortex to resuspend the SPRIselect reagent. Add 10 µL SPRIselect reagent (0.8X) to each sample and pipette mix 15x. Place sample on magnetic separator and remove supernatant. DO NOT discard any beads. Wash twice with freshly prepared 80% ethanol Elute with 50.5 µL Qiagen Buffer EB. Transfer 50 µL to a new strip tube.

Adaptor Ligation Prepare Adaptor Ligation Mix on ice. Pipette mix and centrifuge briefly. Add 50 µL Adaptor Ligation Mix to sample. Pipette mix 15x. Centrifuge briefly. Incubate in a thermocycler to ligate adaptor.

Post Ligation Cleanup --SPRIselect Perform a 0.8X beads purification with SPRIselect reagent Wash twice with freshly prepared 80% ethanol Elute with 30.5 µL Qiagen Buffer EB. Transfer 30 µL to a new strip tube.

Post Sample Index PCR Double Sided Size Selection --SPRIselect Vortex to resuspend the SPRIselect reagent. Add 60 µL SPRIselect reagent (0.6X) to each sample and pipette mix 15x. Incubate 00:05:00 at room temperature. Centrifuge briefly Place sample on magnetic separator. DO NOT discard supernatant. Transfer 150 µL supernatant to a new tube strip tube. Vortex to resuspend the SPRIselect reagent. Add 20 µL SPRIselect reagent (0.8X) to each sample and pipette mix 15x. Incubate 00:05:00 at room temperature. Centrifuge briefly Place sample on magnetic separator and remove supernatant. DO NOT discard any beads. Wash twice with freshly prepared 80% ethanol xi.Elute with 35.5 µL Qiagen Buffer EB. Transfer 35 µL to a new strip tube. Store at 4 °C for up to 72:00:00 or at -20 °C for long-term storage. steps.title: Prepare nuclei from solid tissue
steps.instruction: Isolate single nuclei from solid tissue following the published protocol (steps 1‑14, DOI 10.17504/protocols.io.ufketkw).

steps.title: Dilute nuclei to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the nuclei stock in PBS + 0.1 % BSA to obtain 700–1200 nuclei µL⁻¹ in a final volume of 50 µL. If concentration is low, spin at 900 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend in the appropriate PBS + 0.1 % BSA volume. Use 10 µL for counting and 50 µL for loading. Minimum acceptable is 10 000 nuclei (200 nuclei µL⁻¹ in 50 µL). Do not exceed 0.01 % BSA.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in PBS + RNase inhibitor
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei in 100 µL – 1 mL of PBS containing 0.1 % RNase Inhibitor, adjusting the volume to reach the desired nuclei concentration.

steps.title: Check nuclei integrity
steps.instruction: Examine nuclei under a fluorescent microscope using the DAPI channel. Nuclei should be distinct, rounded, and mostly singlets. If high clumping is observed, re‑filter through a 30‑µm CellTrics filter or discard the sample.

steps.title: Prepare Master Mix on ice
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare the 10X Master Mix, pipette‑mix 15 times, centrifuge briefly, and aliquot 33.4 µL of Master Mix into each well of a PCR 8‑tube strip kept on ice.

steps.title: Load Chromium Single‑Cell B Chip
steps.instruction: 1. Assemble a Chromium Single‑Cell B Chip in a 10X Chip Holder. 2. Load the chip in the order Row 1 → Row 2 → Row 3, avoiding bubbles. 3. Fill unused wells with 50 % glycerol solution: 75 µL in unused Row 1 wells, 40 µL in unused Row 2 wells, 280 µL in unused Row 3 wells. 4. Using the Cell Suspension Volume Calculator, add nuclease‑free water and the appropriate volume of nuclei stock to make a working nuclei suspension (minimum 800 nuclei, maximum 1600 nuclei per reaction). 5. Add 46.6 µL of the working nuclei suspension to each Master Mix tube (total volume = 80 µL). 6. Load 75 µL of the Master Mix + nuclei suspension into the bottom centre of each Row 1 well without bubbles. 7. Snap the Gel Bead strip into a 10X Vortex Adapter, vortex for 30 s, then flick the strip sharply downward; verify no bubbles and even liquid levels. 8. Load 40 µL of gel beads into Row 2 wells (puncture foil only for tubes being used, dispense slowly, no bubbles). 9. Load 280 µL of partitioning oil into each Row 3 well as two 140 µL aliquots. 10. Attach the 10X gasket, align the top notch, ensure gasket holes line up with wells, avoid touching the smooth gasket surface, and do not press down on the gasket.

steps.title: Run Chromium Controller
steps.instruction: Press the eject button to remove the chip, place the assembled chip with gasket in the tray, retract the tray, confirm the program on screen, and press play. The run takes ~7 min; the controller will chime at completion. Proceed immediately to the next step.

steps.title: Transfer GEMs and check volumes
steps.instruction: 1. Chill the strip tubes on ice. 2. Press the eject button to remove the chip and discard the gasket. 3. Open the chip holder, fold the lid back to 45° to expose the wells. 4. Visually inspect volumes in rows 1‑3; abnormally high volume indicates a clog. 5. Slowly aspirate 100 µL of GEMs from the lowest points of the recovery wells without creating a seal between tip and well (GEMs should be opaque and uniform; clear oil in the tip signals a clog). 6. Slowly dispense the aspirated GEMs into the strip tubes on ice, keeping the pipette tip against the sidewall (~20 s).

steps.title: Dynabead cleanup of GEMs
steps.instruction: 1. Add 125 µL Recovery Agent to each sample at room temperature; do NOT mix. 2. Wait 1 min, then carefully aspirate 125 µL of the pink oil phase from the tube bottom without disturbing the aqueous phase. 3. Prepare Dynabeads Cleanup Mix, vortex and centrifuge, then add 200 µL to each sample. 4. Pipette‑mix 5 times, incubate at room temperature for 10 min, then pipette‑mix again for 5 min. 5. Prepare Elution Solution I, vortex and centrifuge briefly. 6. Place the tube on a magnetic separator, remove the supernatant, wash twice with freshly prepared 80 % ethanol, and elute with 35.5 µL Elution Solution I. 7. Transfer 35 µL of eluate to a new strip tube.

steps.title: Run TapeStation for cDNA QC
steps.instruction: Run a TapeStation assay on the amplified cDNA to obtain concentration and size distribution. Expected cDNA size: 400–2500 bp; total yield should be 80–1000 ng. Minimum acceptable total yield is 80 ng.

steps.title: Fragmentation, end‑repair & A‑tailing
steps.instruction: 1. Prepare Fragmentation Mix on ice, vortex and centrifuge briefly. 2. Transfer 10 µL purified cDNA to a new strip tube (this is 25 % of the cDNA; the remaining 30 µL can be stored at 4 °C ≤ 72 h or –20 °C ≤ 4 weeks). 3. Add 25 µL Buffer EB to each sample. 4. Add 15 µL Fragmentation Mix to each sample. 5. Pipette‑mix, centrifuge briefly, and place the tube on a pre‑cooled block. (Skip the hold step to initiate the protocol).

steps.title: MiSeq sequencing QC
steps.instruction: Sequence the library on a MiSeq for QC: Paired‑end, single‑indexing with Read 1 = 28 cycles, i7 = 8 cycles, i5 = 0 cycles, Read 2 = 91 cycles. Load at 11 pM (10X recommended) with optional 1 % PhiX. Expected output: 22–25 million reads.

steps.title: NovaSeq sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the final library on a NovaSeq (target 25 000–50 000 reads per nucleus): Paired‑end, single‑indexing with Read 1 = 28 cycles, i7 = 8 cycles, i5 = 0 cycles, Read 2 = 91 cycles. Load at 300 pM (10X recommended) with optional 1 % PhiX. Expected output per flowcell: SP = 650–800 M reads, S1 = 1.3–1.6 B, S2 = 3.3–4.1 B, S4 = 8–10 B reads.

steps.title: Generate pre‑mRNA reference and sample sheet
steps.instruction: 1. Build a pre‑mRNA reference (required for nuclei experiments to count intronic reads). 2. Use the 10X Sample Sheet Generator to create a SampleSheet.csv. 3. Run the mkfastq command to generate FASTQ files. 4. Run the 10X count pipeline for each sample.
